title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Roasted Asparagus and Garlic Butter
ingredients_json: ["2 pieces Pork loin chop, boneless, raw, 200 g each", "300 g Asparagus, raw", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "30 g Butter, unsalted", "1 dl Lemon juice, fresh", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Trim any excess fat from the pork chops. Pat them dry with paper towels. Season the pork chops generously on both sides with salt and pepper. Toss the asparagus with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Place the seasoned pork chops in a cold, oven-safe skillet. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the skillet. Heat the skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Add the minced garlic and dried thyme to the skillet with the pork chops. Cook for another minute until fragrant. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 8-12 minutes, or until the pork chops reach an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F). While the pork chops are roasting, place the baking sheet with asparagus in the oven as well. Roast the asparagus for 10-12 minutes, until tender-crisp. Once the pork chops are cooked, remove them from the skillet and let them rest for 5 minutes. Add the butter and lemon juice to the skillet with the garlic and thyme. Stir over medium heat until the butter is melted and a sauce forms. Spoon the garlic-lemon butter sauce over the pork chops. Serve the pork chops immediately with the roasted asparagus.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apple and Thyme
ingredients_json: ["400 g Pork loin chops, boneless", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 dl Apple, raw, unspecified, without skin, without core", "2 sprigs Thyme, fresh", "1 dl Onion, raw, unspecified", "1 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "1 g Salt, table", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and season both sides generously with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear the pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side, until nicely browned. Remove the pork chops from the skillet and set aside. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the skillet. Add the diced apple and sliced onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes, until softened and lightly browned. Add the fresh thyme sprigs. Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Stir in the Dijon mustard. Return the pork chops to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Transfer the skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) and bake for 10-15 minutes, or until the pork chops are cooked through and reach an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F). Let the pork chops rest for 5 minutes before serving, spooning the apple and onion sauce over them.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apple and Rosemary
ingredients_json: ["2 pieces Pork loin chop, bone in, raw (approx. 200 g each)", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "1 medium Onion, raw (approx. 150 g)", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "2 medium Apples, raw (approx. 150 g each)", "2 sprigs Rosemary, fresh", "2 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "1 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tsp Dijon mustard", "1/2 tsp Salt, table", "1/4 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once the oil is shimmering, carefully place the pork chops in the skillet and sear for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned. Remove the pork chops from the skillet and set aside. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the sliced onion to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Core the apples and slice them into wedges, then add them to the skillet along with the rosemary sprigs. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until the apples begin to soften. Pour in the chicken broth and apple cider vinegar, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring the mixture to a simmer. Return the pork chops to the skillet, nestling them among the apples and onions. Cover the skillet, reduce the heat to low, and simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, or until the pork chops are cooked through and reach an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F). Stir in the Dijon mustard. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve the pork chops with the apple and onion mixture spooned over the top.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apple-Cranberry Compote and Roasted Brussels Sprouts
ingredients_json: ["2 pieces Pork chops, loin, boneless, raw (approx. 150g each)", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "0.5 tsp Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 dl Fresh cranberries", "1 dl Apple, raw, peeled, cored and diced", "2 tbsp Water", "1 tsp Maple syrup", "0.5 tsp Cinnamon, ground", "300 g Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved", "1 tbsp Balsamic vinegar", "1 clove Garlic, minced"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss the Brussels sprouts with 0.5 tbsp olive oil, balsamic vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. While the sprouts roast, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and season both sides with salt and pepper. Heat the remaining 0.5 tbsp olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork chops for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and cook for another 5-8 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Let the pork chops rest for 5 minutes before serving. Meanwhile, combine the cranberries, diced apple, water, maple syrup, and cinnamon in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the cranberries burst and the compote thickens, about 8-10 minutes. Serve the pan-seared pork chops with the apple-cranberry compote and roasted Brussels sprouts.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apple and Sage Sauce
ingredients_json: ["2 pieces Pork loin chops, bone-in, approx. 200 g each", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 medium Onion, yellow, finely chopped", "2 cloves Garlic, minced", "2 dl Low-sodium chicken broth", "1 dl Unsweetened apple juice", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "1 tsp Fresh sage, chopped", "1 tsp Fresh thyme, chopped", "1/2 tsp Salt", "1/4 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 large Apple, such as Gala or Fuji, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced"]
instructions: Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and season both sides with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown. Remove the chops from the skillet and set aside. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the skillet. Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant. Pour in the chicken broth and apple juice, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer and let it reduce slightly for about 3 minutes. Stir in the Dijon mustard, chopped sage, and chopped thyme. Return the pork chops to the skillet, along with any accumulated juices. Add the sliced apples around the chops. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the pork chops are cooked through and tender, and the apples are softened. Serve the pork chops with the apple and sage sauce spooned over the top.

title: Honey Garlic Baked Pork Ribs with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork spare ribs, raw", "50 ml Honey", "75 ml Soy sauce, low sodium", "30 ml Rice vinegar", "4 cloves Garlic, raw, minced", "15 g Ginger, raw, grated", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "500 g Carrots, raw", "500 g Parsnips, raw", "300 g Sweet potatoes, raw", "1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "0.5 tsp Salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (140°C fan/gas mark 2). Line a baking tray with parchment paper. In a small bowl, whisk together honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, minced garlic, and grated ginger to create the glaze. Place the pork ribs on the prepared baking tray. Brush half of the honey-garlic glaze generously over the ribs. Cover the tray tightly with aluminum foil. Bake for 2 hours. While the ribs are baking, peel and chop the carrots, parsnips, and sweet potatoes into roughly equal-sized chunks. In a large bowl, toss the chopped vegetables with olive oil, salt, and pepper. After 2 hours, carefully remove the foil from the ribs. Increase the oven temperature to 190°C (170°C fan/gas mark 5). Add the seasoned root vegetables to the baking tray around the ribs, ensuring they are in a single layer. Brush the remaining glaze over the ribs. Bake for another 30-40 minutes, or until the ribs are tender and slightly caramelized, and the vegetables are tender and golden brown. Let the ribs rest for 10 minutes before serving with the roasted vegetables.

title: Honey-Glazed Baked Pork Ribs with Rosemary
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork ribs, pork loin ribs", "60 ml Honey", "45 ml Soy sauce", "30 ml Olive oil", "2 cloves Garlic, minced", "1 tbsp Fresh rosemary, chopped", "1 tsp Smoked paprika", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 piece Lemon, for serving"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (320°F). Line a baking tray with parchment paper. In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, smoked paprika, and black pepper to create the glaze. Place the pork ribs on the prepared baking tray. Generously brush the glaze all over the ribs, ensuring they are well coated. Cover the tray tightly with aluminum foil. Bake for 2.5 hours, or until the pork is tender and almost falling off the bone. Remove the foil for the last 30 minutes of cooking to allow the glaze to caramelize. Once cooked, let the ribs rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve hot with wedges of fresh lemon.

title: Honey-Garlic Glazed Pork Ribs with Roasted Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork ribs, spare ribs", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tsp Paprika, sweet", "0.5 tsp Garlic powder", "0.5 tsp Onion powder", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Salt", "1 dl Honey", "0.5 dl Soy sauce, low sodium", "4 cloves Garlic, minced", "1 tbsp Ginger, fresh, grated", "1 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "500 g Sweet potatoes, cubed", "1 dl Broccoli florets", "1 dl Red bell pepper, chopped"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Pat the pork ribs dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix together olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and salt. Rub this mixture all over the pork ribs. Place the ribs on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Roast for 1 hour, or until they are starting to become tender. While the ribs are roasting, prepare the glaze. In a small saucepan, combine honey, soy sauce, minced garlic, grated ginger, and apple cider vinegar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the honey is dissolved and the glaze has thickened slightly, about 5-7 minutes. After the initial hour of roasting, remove the ribs from the oven. Brush them generously with the honey-garlic glaze. Add the cubed sweet potatoes, broccoli florets, and chopped red bell pepper to the same baking sheet around the ribs. Drizzle the vegetables with a little extra olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Return the baking sheet to the oven and continue roasting for another 30-40 minutes, or until the ribs are fully cooked, tender, and slightly caramelized, and the vegetables are tender and roasted. Baste the ribs with the glaze one more time during the last 10 minutes of cooking. Let the ribs rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing and serving with the roasted vegetables.

title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Pork Ribs with Roasted Broccoli
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork ribs, spare ribs", "1 dl Soy sauce, low sodium", "1 dl Honey", "0.5 dl Apple cider vinegar", "3 cloves Garlic, minced", "1 tbsp Ginger, grated", "1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "500 g Broccoli florets", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "0.5 tsp Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Place the pork ribs in a slow cooker. In a separate bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, honey, apple cider vinegar, minced garlic, grated ginger, and 1 tsp of black pepper. Pour this marinade over the ribs, ensuring they are well coated. Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 3-4 hours, until the pork is tender. About 30 minutes before serving, preheat your oven to 200°C (180°C fan/Gas Mark 6). Toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, salt, and 0.25 tsp black pepper on a baking sheet. Roast the broccoli for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly charred. Once the ribs are cooked, carefully remove them from the slow cooker. You can serve them as is, or for a slightly caramelized finish, place them under a hot grill for 2-3 minutes per side until browned. Serve the ribs hot with the roasted broccoli on the side.

title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Pork Ribs with Roasted Broccoli
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork ribs, spare ribs", "2 dl Honey", "1 dl Soy sauce, low sodium", "0.5 dl Apple cider vinegar", "4 cloves Garlic, minced", "1 tbsp Ginger, grated", "1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "500 g Broccoli florets", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "0.5 tsp Salt"]
instructions: Place the pork ribs in your slow cooker. In a separate bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, minced garlic, grated ginger, and black pepper. Pour the sauce over the ribs, ensuring they are well coated. Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours, or on high for 3-4 hours, until the pork is tender.  Preheat your oven to 200°C. Toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until tender and slightly charred. Once the ribs are cooked, remove them from the slow cooker and either broil them for a few minutes to crisp up the edges or serve them directly with the roasted broccoli.

title: Slow Cooker Balsamic Glazed Pork Shoulder with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1500 g Pork shoulder, boneless", "2 dl Balsamic vinegar", "1 dl Beef broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Honey", "2 cloves Garlic, minced", "1 tsp Dried rosemary", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "500 g Carrots, peeled and cut into chunks", "500 g Parsnips, peeled and cut into chunks", "200 g Onion, red, cut into wedges", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Salt"]
instructions: Place the pork shoulder in the slow cooker. In a medium bowl, whisk together the balsamic vinegar, beef broth, honey, minced garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Pour this mixture over the pork shoulder. Cover and cook on low for 8 hours or on high for 4-5 hours, or until the pork is tender and easily shreds with a fork.  About 30 minutes before the pork is done, preheat your oven to 200 degrees C (400 degrees F). Toss the chopped carrots, parsnips, and onion wedges with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a large baking sheet. Spread them out in a single layer. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized, flipping halfway through. Once the pork is cooked, carefully remove it from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks. Skim off any excess fat from the cooking liquid in the slow cooker, then place the slow cooker on the stovetop over medium-high heat. Bring the liquid to a simmer and let it reduce for about 5-10 minutes until it thickens into a glaze. Serve the shredded pork alongside the roasted root vegetables, drizzled with the balsamic glaze.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork Shoulder with Apple Cider Glaze
ingredients_json: ["1500 g Pork shoulder, boneless", "2 dl Apple cider", "1 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Brown sugar, light", "1 tsp Smoked paprika", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "0.5 tsp Onion powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "0.25 tsp Cayenne pepper", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 medium Onion, yellow, chopped", "2 cloves Garlic, minced"]
instructions: Pat the pork shoulder dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the pork shoulder on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the pork from the skillet and set aside. Add the chopped onion to the skillet and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Deglaze the pan by pouring in the apple cider vinegar and scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Let it simmer for 1 minute. Pour in the apple cider and chicken broth, and stir in the brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne pepper. Return the seared pork shoulder to the skillet, ensuring it is partially submerged in the liquid. Cover the skillet tightly with a lid or aluminum foil and transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Cook for 4-6 hours, or until the pork is fork-tender and shreds easily. Once cooked, carefully remove the pork from the skillet and place it on a cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork. Skim off any excess fat from the cooking liquid in the skillet. If desired, simmer the sauce over medium heat for 5-10 minutes to thicken slightly. Return the shredded pork to the skillet and toss to coat with the glaze. Serve hot.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork with Apple Cider Glaze
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork shoulder, bone out", "2 dl Apple cider", "1 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Smoked paprika", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "1 tsp Onion powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "0.5 tsp Salt", "2 tbsp Maple syrup", "1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce", "2 Whole grain buns"]
instructions: Place the pork shoulder in your slow cooker. In a medium bowl, whisk together the apple cider, chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and salt. Pour this mixture over the pork shoulder. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours, or until the pork is fork-tender and easily shreds. Remove the pork from the slow cooker and place it on a cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork. Skim any excess fat from the cooking liquid in the slow cooker. Stir in the maple syrup and Worcestershire sauce into the cooking liquid and bring to a simmer on the stovetop over medium heat. Cook for about 5-10 minutes, or until slightly thickened to create a glaze. Return the shredded pork to the slow cooker and toss with the glaze until well coated. Serve the pulled pork on whole grain buns.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork Shoulder with Apple Cider Glaze
ingredients_json: ["1500 g Pork shoulder, boneless", "2 dl Apple cider", "1 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Brown sugar, packed", "1 tbsp Smoked paprika", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "1 tsp Onion powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "0.5 tsp Salt", "2 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "200 g Onion, yellow, sliced", "15 g Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish"]
instructions: Place the pork shoulder in a slow cooker. In a medium bowl, whisk together the apple cider, chicken broth, brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and salt. Pour this mixture over the pork shoulder. Add the sliced onion around the pork. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours, or on high for 4-5 hours, until the pork is very tender and shreds easily with a fork. Remove the pork from the slow cooker and place it on a cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork, discarding any excess fat. Drain most of the liquid from the slow cooker, reserving about 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid. Return the shredded pork to the slow cooker. In a small bowl, whisk together the reserved cooking liquid, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, and Dijon mustard. Pour this glaze over the shredded pork and stir to combine. Cook on high for another 30 minutes, uncovered, to allow the glaze to thicken and coat the pork. Stir occasionally. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork with Apple Cider Slaw
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork shoulder, bone out", "2 dl Apple cider", "1 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 unit Onion, yellow, large", "4 cloves Garlic, raw", "2 tbsp Paprika, sweet", "1 tbsp Cumin, ground", "1 tsp Cayenne pepper", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Salt", "1 bag Coleslaw mix, 450 g", "1 dl Mayonnaise", "2 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "0.5 tsp Salt", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 150°C (300°F). Pat the pork shoulder dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the pork shoulder on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the pork and set aside. Add the chopped onion to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the paprika, cumin, and cayenne pepper, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the apple cider and chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Return the pork shoulder to the pot, submerging it as much as possible in the liquid. Cover the pot tightly and transfer it to the preheated oven. Cook for 4-5 hours, or until the pork is fork-tender and easily shreds. Remove the pork from the pot and let it rest for 10 minutes before shredding it with two forks. While the pork rests, prepare the slaw: In a large bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Add the coleslaw mix and toss to combine. Serve the shredded pork piled high on buns, topped with the apple cider slaw.

title: Herb-Crusted Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Asparagus and Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_json: ["500 g Pork tenderloin, trimmed", "300 g Sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed", "400 g Asparagus, trimmed", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "1 tbsp Fresh rosemary, chopped", "1 tbsp Fresh thyme, chopped", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper", "1.5 tsp Salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss the cubed sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, half of the salt, and half of the pepper in a baking dish. Roast for 15 minutes. While the sweet potatoes are roasting, pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine the Dijon mustard, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, garlic powder, and the remaining salt and pepper. Rub this mixture all over the pork tenderloin. After the sweet potatoes have roasted for 15 minutes, add the trimmed asparagus to the baking dish, tossing it with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Place the herb-crusted pork tenderloin in the center of the baking dish amongst the vegetables. Return the dish to the oven and roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) and the vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized. Let the pork rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing and serving with the roasted vegetables.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Tenderloin with Apple-Cranberry Compote and Roasted Brussels Sprouts
ingredients_json: ["500 g Pork tenderloin, trimmed", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "0.5 tsp Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground", "250 g Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "0.25 tsp Salt", "0.12 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 large Apple, peeled, cored, and diced", "50 g Dried cranberries", "50 ml Water", "1 tbsp Maple syrup", "0.5 tsp Cinnamon, ground", "0.25 tsp Nutmeg, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss the halved Brussels sprouts with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 0.25 teaspoon of salt, and 0.12 teaspoon of black pepper on a baking sheet. Spread them in a single layer and roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. While the Brussels sprouts are roasting, pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels. Season it all over with 0.5 teaspoon of salt and 0.25 teaspoon of black pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork tenderloin for 2-3 minutes per side, until nicely browned. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and continue cooking for 12-15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Remove the pork from the skillet and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing. While the pork is resting, combine the diced apple, dried cranberries, water, maple syrup, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apples are tender and the compote has thickened slightly. Slice the rested pork tenderloin and serve with the roasted Brussels sprouts and apple-cranberry compote.

title: Lemon Herb Roasted Pork Tenderloin with Asparagus and Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_json: ["600 g Pork tenderloin, trimmed", "400 g Sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed", "400 g Asparagus, trimmed", "3 tbsp Olive oil", "2 tbsp Fresh lemon juice", "2 cloves Garlic, minced", "1 tbsp Fresh rosemary, chopped", "1 tbsp Fresh thyme, chopped", "1 tsp Salt", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200 degrees Celsius. Toss the cubed sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes. While the sweet potatoes are roasting, prepare the pork tenderloin. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper. Place the pork tenderloin in a bowl or on a plate and pour the herb mixture over it, coating it evenly. Once the sweet potatoes have roasted for 20 minutes, add the trimmed asparagus to the same baking sheet, tossing them with the sweet potatoes. Make space on the baking sheet and place the seasoned pork tenderloin among the vegetables. Return the baking sheet to the oven and roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63 degrees Celsius and the vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized. Let the pork rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Serve the sliced pork tenderloin with the roasted asparagus and sweet potatoes.

title: Herb-Crusted Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Pork tenderloin, trimmed", "300 g Carrots, peeled", "300 g Parsnips, peeled", "200 g Sweet potatoes, peeled", "100 g Red onion, peeled", "4 cloves Garlic, unpeeled", "3 tbsp Olive oil", "2 tbsp Fresh rosemary, chopped", "2 tbsp Fresh thyme, chopped", "1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1.5 tsp Salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (180°C fan/gas mark 6). Toss the chopped carrots, parsnips, sweet potatoes, and red onion wedges with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, half of the rosemary and thyme, salt, and pepper on a large baking sheet. Arrange the vegetables in a single layer. Pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil with the remaining rosemary and thyme, salt, and pepper. Rub this mixture all over the pork tenderloin. Place the pork tenderloin on top of the vegetables in the baking sheet. Add the unpeeled garlic cloves amongst the vegetables. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) and the vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized. Let the pork rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve the sliced pork tenderloin with the roasted root vegetables.

title: Herb-Crusted Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["500 g Pork tenderloin", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tbsp Dried rosemary", "1 tbsp Dried thyme", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper", "1 tsp Salt", "400 g Carrots, raw", "300 g Parsnips, raw", "200 g Sweet potatoes, raw", "1 medium Onion, yellow"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (180°C fan/Gas Mark 6). Pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, rosemary, thyme, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt. Rub this mixture all over the pork tenderloin. Cut the carrots, parsnips, sweet potatoes, and onion into roughly equal-sized chunks. Place the chopped vegetables in a large roasting pan. Drizzle the vegetables with a little extra olive oil (about 1 tbsp) and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss to coat. Place the seasoned pork tenderloin on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) and the vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized. Let the pork rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing.

title: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Pot Pie with Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["400 g Lentils, brown, dry", "1 kg Mixed vegetables, frozen (carrots, peas, corn, green beans)", "250 g Onion, yellow, raw", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "50 g Celery, raw", "30 g Olive oil", "8 dl Vegetable broth, low sodium", "50 g Whole wheat flour", "2 tbsp Tomato paste", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "0.5 tsp Dried rosemary", "1 pinch Black pepper, ground", "0.5 tsp Salt", "300 g Whole wheat flour", "150 g Butter, unsalted, cold", "1 dl Cold water", "1 piece Egg, raw (for egg wash)"]
instructions: Rinse the dry lentils thoroughly and set aside. Finely chop the onion, garlic, and celery. Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and celery and sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Sprinkle in the whole wheat flour and stir to coat the vegetables, cooking for 1-2 minutes to form a roux. Gradually whisk in the vegetable broth, ensuring no lumps form. Bring the mixture to a simmer. Add the rinsed lentils, frozen mixed vegetables, thyme, and rosemary. Season with salt and pepper. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the sauce has thickened. While the filling simmers, prepare the crust. In a medium bowl, combine the 300g whole wheat flour and a pinch of salt. Cut in the cold butter using a pastry blender or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add the cold water, 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Divide the dough in half, flatten each half into a disc, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Divide the lentil and vegetable filling into individual oven-safe ramekins or one larger pie dish. Roll out one disc of dough and place it over the filling, crimping the edges to seal. Cut a few slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape. If using a second disc for a lid, roll it out and place it on top, sealing and venting. Brush the top crust with a beaten egg for a golden finish. Place the pot pies on a baking sheet to catch any drips. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.

title: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Pot Pie
ingredients_json: ["600 g Chicken fillet, raw", "15 g Olive oil", "200 g Onion, raw", "200 g Carrot, raw", "200 g Celery, raw", "100 g Peas, frozen", "50 g All-purpose flour", "4 dl Milk, semi-skimmed, 1.5% fat", "1 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "1 tsp Salt, table", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tbsp Fresh thyme, chopped", "2 sheets Puff pastry, ready-made", "1 piece Egg, raw"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200 degrees Celsius (180 degrees Celsius fan/gas mark 6). Cut the chicken fillet into bite-sized pieces and season with half the salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet or pot over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until browned on all sides, then remove from the skillet and set aside. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir well, cooking for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and chicken broth until smooth. Bring the mixture to a simmer, stirring constantly, until it thickens. Stir in the cooked chicken, frozen peas, remaining salt and pepper, and fresh thyme. Cook for another 2 minutes until heated through. Pour the filling into individual oven-safe ramekins or one larger pie dish. Unroll the puff pastry sheets and cut them to fit the tops of your ramekins or dish. Crimp the edges to seal. Whisk the egg in a small bowl and brush it over the puff pastry tops for a golden finish. Cut a few slits in the pastry to allow steam to escape. Place the pot pies on a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed up, and the filling is bubbling.

title: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Pot Pie with Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["400 g Brown lentils, dry", "1.5 l Vegetable broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "2 medium Onions, yellow, chopped", "4 medium Carrots, peeled and diced", "3 stalks Celery, diced", "2 cloves Garlic, minced", "100 g Peas, frozen", "50 g Corn, frozen", "2 tbsp All-purpose flour, whole wheat", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "0.5 tsp Dried rosemary, crushed", "1 pinch Black pepper, ground", "2 sheets Puff pastry, whole wheat", "1 piece Egg, beaten (for egg wash)"]
instructions: Rinse the dry brown lentils thoroughly. In a large pot or Dutch oven, combine the rinsed lentils with 1.5 liters of low-sodium vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. While the lentils are cooking, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onions, diced carrots, and diced celery. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, until the vegetables begin to soften. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux. Add the cooked lentils and their cooking liquid to the skillet with the vegetables. Stir in the frozen peas, frozen corn, dried thyme, dried rosemary, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the filling has thickened. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Divide the lentil and vegetable filling among four individual oven-safe ramekins or small pie dishes. Cut out circles of whole wheat puff pastry to fit the tops of the ramekins. Place a puff pastry circle over the filling in each ramekin, pressing the edges to seal. You can crimp the edges with a fork if desired. Make a small slit in the center of each pastry top to allow steam to escape. Brush the tops of the pastry with the beaten egg wash for a golden finish. Place the filled ramekins on a baking sheet to catch any drips. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the pastry is puffed up and golden brown, and the filling is bubbly.

title: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Pot Pie with Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["400 g Chicken breast, cooked, shredded", "150 g Carrot, raw, diced", "150 g Celery, raw, diced", "100 g Onion, raw, diced", "50 g Peas, frozen", "30 g Butter, unsalted", "30 g Whole wheat flour", "4 dl Low-sodium chicken broth", "1 dl Milk, semi-skimmed, 1.5% fat", "1 tsp Thyme, dried", "0.5 tsp Rosemary, dried", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "200 g Whole wheat flour, for crust", "100 g Butter, cold, diced, for crust", "0.5 dl Water, ice cold, for crust", "0.5 tsp Salt, for crust"]
instructions: For the filling: Melt 30g butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery and cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in 30g whole wheat flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 5 minutes. Stir in shredded chicken, frozen peas, dried thyme, rosemary, and black pepper. Remove from heat and let cool slightly. For the crust: In a large bowl, combine 200g whole wheat flour and 0.5 tsp salt. Cut in 100g cold diced butter using a pastry blender or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add 0.5 dl ice cold water, mixing until just combined. Do not overmix. Divide the dough in half, flatten into discs, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disc of dough to fit the bottom of a 23cm pie dish. Pour the chicken and vegetable filling into the dish. Roll out the second disc of dough to fit the top of the pie. Crimp the edges to seal and cut a few slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Pot Pie
ingredients_json: ["200 g Brown lentils, dry", "1 kg Mixed root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, potatoes), peeled and diced", "200 g Onion, yellow, chopped", "100 g Celery, chopped", "2 cloves Garlic, minced", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 dl Vegetable broth", "1 dl Red wine", "2 tbsp Tomato paste", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "1 tsp Dried rosemary", "150 g All-purpose flour", "100 g Butter, unsalted, cold and cubed", "50 ml Cold water", "1 piece Egg, beaten (for egg wash)"]
instructions: Rinse the brown lentils thoroughly. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and celery and sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the diced root vegetables, rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, red wine, tomato paste, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper to taste. While the filling simmers, prepare the pastry. In a medium bowl, combine the flour and butter. Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to cut the butter into the flour until it resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add the cold water, mixing until the dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Divide the dough in half, flatten each half into a disk, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Once the filling is cooked and vegetables are tender, pour it into individual oven-safe ramekins or one larger pie dish. Roll out one disk of pastry and place it over the filling, trimming and crimping the edges. Cut a few vents in the top crust. Roll out the second disk and cut out decorative shapes or strips to place on top, if desired. Brush the pastry with the beaten egg wash. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.

title: Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Pot Roast
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Beef chuck roast", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "2 large Onions, chopped", "4 cloves Garlic, minced", "500 g Carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks", "400 g Potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks", "200 g Celery, cut into 1-inch pieces", "1 dl Dry red wine", "1 liter Beef broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Tomato paste", "2 Bay leaves", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "1 tsp Dried rosemary", "Salt, to taste", "Black pepper, to taste"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Pat the beef chuck roast dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the beef on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the beef and set aside. Add the chopped onions to the pot and cook until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the carrots, potatoes, and celery to the pot and stir to combine with the onions. title: Hearty Vegetable and Lean Beef Pot Roast

title: Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Pot Roast

title: Hearty Balsamic Pot Roast with Root Vegetables

title: Creamy Leek and Potato Soup with Smoked Paprika
ingredients_json: ["800 g Potatoes, waxy, raw", "300 g Leek, raw", "1 dl Onion, raw", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1.2 l Vegetable broth", "2 dl Milk, semi-skimmed, unspecified", "1 tsp Salt", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Smoked paprika"]

title: Creamy Leek and Potato Soup with Herbs
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Potatoes, starchy, e.g. King Edward", "400 g Leeks, white and light green parts only", "1.5 l Vegetable broth", "2 dl Milk, semi-skimmed", "50 g Butter", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "1 sprig Fresh thyme", "1 sprig Fresh rosemary", "2 tbsp Fresh parsley, chopped", "1 tsp Salt", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into roughly 2 cm cubes. Wash the leeks thoroughly to remove any grit, trim them, and slice them thinly. Mince the garlic. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the sliced leeks and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Pour in the vegetable broth, add the cubed potatoes, thyme sprig, and rosemary sprig. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 20-25 minutes, or until the potatoes are very tender. Remove and discard the herb sprigs. Carefully transfer the soup to a blender in batches (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot) and blend until smooth and creamy. Return the soup to the pot if using a standard blender. Stir in the semi-skimmed milk. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Heat gently without boiling. Stir in the fresh chopped parsley just before serving.

title: Creamy Leek and Potato Soup with Smoked Paprika
ingredients_json: ["1000 g Potatoes, starchy, white, raw", "500 g Leeks, white and light green parts only, raw", "20 g Olive oil", "1200 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "200 ml Milk, semi-skimmed, 1.5% fat", "2 g Salt, table", "1 g Black pepper, ground", "5 g Smoked paprika"]
instructions: Peel and dice the potatoes into roughly 2 cm cubes. Wash the leeks thoroughly to remove any grit and slice them thinly. Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced leeks and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Do not let them brown. Add the diced potatoes and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork-tender. Carefully transfer about half of the soup to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot). Blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot with the remaining chunky soup. Stir in the milk, salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. Heat gently over low heat for another 5 minutes, ensuring it doesn't boil. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve hot.

title: Creamy Leek and Potato Soup with Fresh Herbs
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Potatoes, starchy, like Maris Piper or Russet", "300 g Leeks, white and light green parts only", "1.2 l Vegetable broth, low sodium", "2 dl Milk, semi-skimmed", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 piece Garlic, clove", "1 tbsp Fresh chives, chopped", "1 tbsp Fresh parsley, chopped", "1 tsp Salt, fine", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into roughly 2 cm cubes. Wash the leeks thoroughly to remove any grit, then slice them thinly. Mince the garlic. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced leeks and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the cubed potatoes and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the potatoes are very tender. Carefully transfer about half of the soup to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot) and blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot, stir in the milk, and heat gently over low heat without boiling. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in most of the chopped chives and parsley. Serve hot, garnished with the remaining fresh herbs.

title: Creamy Leek and Potato Soup with Smoked Paprika
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Potatoes, starchy, raw", "500 g Leeks, raw", "1 piece Onion, yellow, raw", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "1.5 liter Vegetable broth", "2 dl Milk, semi-skimmed", "3 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tsp Smoked paprika", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "10 g Fresh parsley, chopped"]
instructions: Peel and dice the potatoes into roughly 2 cm cubes. Thoroughly wash the leeks to remove any grit, then slice them thinly. Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the sliced leeks and minced garlic, and cook for another 5 minutes until the leeks are tender. Stir in the smoked paprika and black pepper, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the diced potatoes and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork-tender. Carefully transfer about half of the soup to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot) and blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot. Stir in the milk and heat gently over low heat until warmed through, being careful not to boil. Season with salt to taste, if needed. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a drizzle of the remaining olive oil.

title: Rosemary Garlic Crusted Prime Rib Roast
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Beef, prime rib roast, bone-in", "3 tbsp Olive oil", "2 tbsp Rosemary, dried", "1 tbsp Garlic powder", "1 tbsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Salt, kosher", "2 dl Water"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Pat the prime rib roast dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, dried rosemary, garlic powder, black pepper, and kosher salt to create a paste. Rub this mixture all over the prime rib roast. Place the roast, fat-side up, on a rack in a roasting pan. Add 2 dl of water to the bottom of the pan to help create steam. Sear the roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 160°C (325°F) and continue roasting for approximately 12-15 minutes per 500g for medium-rare (internal temperature of 55-57°C or 131-135°F), or longer for your desired doneness. Use a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the roast, avoiding the bone. Once the roast reaches your desired temperature, remove it from the oven, tent loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20 minutes before carving. This resting period is crucial for juicy meat.

title: Classic Herb-Crusted Prime Rib Roast with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1800 g Beef rib roast, bone-in", "3 tbsp Olive oil", "2 tbsp Rosemary, dried, crushed", "2 tbsp Thyme, dried, crushed", "1 tbsp Garlic powder", "1 tbsp Onion powder", "1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Salt, fine", "600 g Potatoes, raw, flesh, unspecified", "400 g Carrots, raw", "300 g Parsnips, raw", "2 dl Beef broth, low sodium", "2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C. Pat the beef rib roast completely dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix together the olive oil, dried rosemary, dried thyme, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and salt to create a paste. Rub this herb paste all over the prime rib. Place the roast, fat side up, in a roasting pan. Roast at 220°C for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 160°C and continue roasting for approximately 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, or until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part (not touching bone) registers 50°C for medium-rare. While the roast is cooking, prepare the vegetables. Peel and chop the potatoes, carrots, and parsnips into roughly equal-sized chunks. Toss them in a bowl with a little olive oil, salt, and pepper. About 45 minutes before the roast is done, scatter the vegetables around the roast in the pan. In a small bowl, whisk together the beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, and Dijon mustard for the au jus. After the roast has reached your desired temperature, carefully remove it from the roasting pan and let it rest on a cutting board, loosely tented with foil, for at least 20 minutes before carving. While the roast is resting, place the roasting pan with the vegetables and juices over medium heat on the stovetop. Add the prepared au jus mixture to the pan, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer gently for 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Serve the carved prime rib with the roasted root vegetables and the pan juices.

title: Herb-Crusted Prime Rib Roast with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1500 g Beef, standing rib roast", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "3 cloves Garlic, fresh", "1 tbsp Rosemary, dried", "1 tbsp Thyme, dried", "1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tsp Salt, fine sea salt", "500 g Carrots, raw", "500 g Parsnips, raw", "300 g Potatoes, raw", "2 dl Beef broth, low sodium"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C. Pat the prime rib dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix together the olive oil, minced garlic, dried rosemary, dried thyme, black pepper, and salt to form a paste. Rub this paste all over the prime rib. Place the roast, fat side up, in a roasting pan. Add the chopped carrots, parsnips, and potatoes around the roast. Pour the beef broth into the bottom of the roasting pan. Place the roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Then, reduce the oven temperature to 160°C and continue roasting for approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes to 2 hours, or until an internal meat thermometer reads 55°C for medium-rare. For medium, aim for 60°C. Let the roast rest for at least 15-20 minutes before carving. Serve the prime rib with the roasted root vegetables.

title: Herb-Crusted Prime Rib Roast with Garlic and Rosemary
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Beef roast, rib, boneless", "30 g Olive oil", "15 g Garlic, raw", "10 g Rosemary, fresh", "5 g Thyme, fresh", "10 g Salt, table", "5 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C. Pat the beef roast completely dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, finely chop the garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Mix this herb mixture with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper to form a paste. Rub this paste all over the prime rib roast, ensuring it's evenly coated. Place the roast fat-side up on a wire rack in a roasting pan. Sear the roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Then, reduce the oven temperature to 160°C and continue roasting for about 1.5 to 2 hours, or until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part registers 52°C for rare, 57°C for medium-rare, or 63°C for medium. Let the roast rest for 20-30 minutes, loosely tented with foil, before carving. This resting period is crucial for juices to redistribute, resulting in a more tender and flavorful roast.

title: Herb-Crusted Prime Rib Roast with Roasted Garlic Potatoes
ingredients_json: ["1500 g Beef, rib roast, boneless", "3 tbsp Olive oil", "3 cloves Garlic, raw", "2 tbsp Rosemary, dried", "1 tbsp Thyme, dried", "1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1.5 tsp Salt, fine sea salt", "1 kg Potatoes, all-purpose, whole", "3 tbsp Butter, unsalted", "0.5 dl Parsley, fresh, chopped"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 230°C. Pat the prime rib dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix together 2 tablespoons of olive oil, chopped garlic, dried rosemary, dried thyme, black pepper, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub this mixture all over the beef roast. Place the roast, fat side up, in a roasting pan. Insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part of the roast, avoiding the bone. Roast at 230°C for 15 minutes. Then, reduce the oven temperature to 160°C and continue roasting for about 12-15 minutes per pound (or 25-30 minutes per kilogram) for medium-rare, or until the internal temperature reaches your desired doneness (52°C for medium-rare). While the roast is cooking, wash and cut the potatoes into bite-sized pieces. Toss them with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, melted butter, 0.5 teaspoon of salt, and chopped parsley. Spread the potatoes on a baking sheet. About 45 minutes before the roast is expected to be done, place the potatoes in the oven. Roast until tender and golden brown. Once the prime rib reaches the desired temperature, remove it from the oven, tent loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20 minutes before carving. Serve the carved prime rib with the roasted potatoes.

title: Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pulled Pork
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork shoulder, boneless", "5 dl Apple cider, unfiltered", "2 dl Onion, yellow, chopped", "4 cloves Garlic, minced", "2 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Smoked paprika", "1 tsp Cumin, ground", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "0.5 tsp Salt", "2 tbsp Olive oil"]
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork shoulder on all sides until nicely browned, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer the pork to a slow cooker. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet and sauté for about 2 minutes until softened. Deglaze the skillet with the apple cider vinegar, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Pour the apple cider into the slow cooker. Add the smoked paprika, ground cumin, black pepper, and salt. Stir to combine. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours, or on high for 4-5 hours, until the pork is very tender and shreds easily with a fork. Remove the pork from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks. Return the shredded pork to the slow cooker and toss with the cooking liquid. Serve warm.

title: Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pulled Pork with Coleslaw
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork shoulder, boneless", "4 dl Apple cider", "2 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "1 dl Onion, yellow, chopped", "4 cloves Garlic, minced", "2 tbsp Brown sugar, light", "1 tbsp Smoked paprika", "1 tsp Cumin, ground", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "0.5 tsp Salt", "1 kg Cabbage, shredded", "2 dl Carrot, shredded", "1 dl Red onion, thinly sliced", "1.5 dl Mayonnaise", "2 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "1 tsp Sugar", "0.5 tsp Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Place the pork shoulder in a slow cooker. In a bowl, whisk together the apple cider, chicken broth, chopped yellow onion, minced garlic, brown sugar, smoked paprika, cumin, black pepper, and salt. Pour this mixture over the pork. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours, or on high for 4-5 hours, until the pork is tender and easily shreds. Remove the pork from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks. Skim any excess fat from the cooking liquid and return the shredded pork to the slow cooker, tossing it in the reduced sauce. For the coleslaw, in a large bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, and thinly sliced red onion. In a separate small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, sugar, salt, and black pepper. Pour the dressing over the cabbage mixture and toss to combine. Serve the pulled pork warm, topped with coleslaw.

title: Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pulled Pork with Coleslaw
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Pork shoulder, boneless", "240 ml Apple cider", "120 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "60 ml Soy sauce, low sodium", "30 ml Maple syrup", "2 cloves Garlic, minced", "1 tsp Smoked paprika", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 small Onion, sliced", "200 g Cabbage, shredded", "100 g Carrot, shredded", "60 ml Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "30 ml Apple cider vinegar", "15 ml Dijon mustard", "5 g Fresh parsley, chopped"]
instructions: Place the pork shoulder in a slow cooker. In a bowl, whisk together apple cider, chicken broth, soy sauce, maple syrup, minced garlic, smoked paprika, and black pepper. Pour the liquid mixture over the pork. Add the sliced onion on top. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours or on high for 4-5 hours, until the pork is tender and easily shreds with a fork. Remove the pork from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks. Skim any excess fat from the cooking liquid and return the shredded pork to the slow cooker. Stir to coat the pork in the sauce. For the coleslaw, combine shredded cabbage and carrot in a bowl. In a separate small bowl, whisk together Greek yogurt, apple cider vinegar, and Dijon mustard. Pour the dressing over the cabbage and carrot mixture and toss to combine. Stir in fresh parsley. Serve the pulled pork on its own or with the coleslaw.

title: Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pulled Pork
ingredients_json: ["1500 g Pork shoulder, boneless", "5 dl Apple cider, unsweetened", "1 dl Onion, yellow, raw", "2 tbsp Brown sugar, light", "1 tbsp Paprika, ground", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "1 tsp Salt, sea", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "2 dl Cabbage, white, raw"]
instructions: Trim any excess fat from the pork shoulder. Place the pork shoulder in a slow cooker. In a bowl, whisk together the apple cider, chopped yellow onion, brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, sea salt, and black pepper. Pour this mixture over the pork shoulder in the slow cooker. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours, or on high for 4-5 hours, until the pork is tender and easily shredded. Once cooked, remove the pork from the slow cooker and place it on a cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork. Skim any excess fat from the cooking liquid in the slow cooker and return the shredded pork to the liquid, stirring to coat. Serve the pulled pork warm, optionally with a side of shredded raw cabbage for a fresh crunch.

title: Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pulled Pork with Coleslaw
ingredients_json: ["1500 g Pork shoulder, bone out", "5 dl Apple cider", "1 dl Apple cider vinegar", "2 tbsp Smoked paprika", "1 tbsp Brown sugar, light", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "1 tsp Onion powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "1 kg Cabbage, white, shredded", "200 g Carrot, grated", "150 g Mayonnaise", "2 tbsp White wine vinegar", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "0.5 tsp Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Place the pork shoulder in your slow cooker. In a medium bowl, whisk together the apple cider, apple cider vinegar, smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, and 0.5 tsp of black pepper. Pour this mixture over the pork. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours or on high for 4-5 hours, until the pork is very tender and easily shreds with a fork. Remove the pork from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks, discarding any excess fat. Return the shredded pork to the slow cooker and stir it into the cooking liquid.
