Arrange the thinly sliced apples over the caramel mixture in a decorative pattern. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, almond flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. In a separate bowl, beat the eggs, then whisk in the Greek yogurt, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and the remaining 75g of melted butter. Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, mixing until just combined. Stir in the milk to achieve a smooth batter consistency. Pour the batter carefully over the apples in the cake tin, spreading it evenly. Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the cake cool in the tin for 10 minutes before carefully inverting it onto a serving plate. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Healthy Pear and Ginger Upside-Down Cake
ingredients_json: ["200 g Pears, ripe, any variety", "50 g Maple syrup", "25 g Butter, unsalted", "10 g Fresh ginger, grated", "150 g Whole wheat flour", "100 g Oats, rolled", "75 g Erythritol", "1 tsp Baking powder", "0.5 tsp Ground cinnamon", "0.25 tsp Ground nutmeg", "2 large Eggs, raw", "60 ml Milk, low-fat (1.5%)", "60 ml Vegetable oil, rapeseed", "1 tsp Vanilla extract"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (160°C fan/Gas Mark 4). Peel, core, and slice the pears. In a small saucepan, gently heat the maple syrup, butter, and grated ginger until the butter is melted and the mixture is combined. Pour this mixture into the base of an 18-20 cm round cake tin, spreading it evenly. Arrange the pear slices on top of the maple syrup mixture in a decorative pattern. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, rolled oats, erythritol, baking powder, cinnamon, and nutmeg. In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract until well combined. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined, being careful not to overmix. Spoon the batter evenly over the pear layer in the cake tin. Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean. Let the cake cool in the tin for 10 minutes before carefully inverting it onto a serving plate. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Whole Wheat Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Whoopie Pies
ingredients_json: ["150 g Whole wheat flour", "100 g Rolled oats", "50 g Almond flour", "5 g Baking soda", "2 g Salt", "100 g Unsalted butter, softened", "150 g Maple syrup", "2 large Egg, room temperature", "10 ml Vanilla extract", "100 g Dark chocolate chips (70% cacao)"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F). Line baking sheets with parchment paper. In a medium bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, rolled oats, almond flour, baking soda, and salt. In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and maple syrup until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. Fold in the dark chocolate chips. Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 5 cm (2 inches) between them. Bake for 9-11 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the centers are set. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. Once cooled, spread your favorite healthy cream filling on the flat side of one cookie and top with another.

title: Whole Wheat Chocolate Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Frosting
ingredients_json: ["150 g Whole wheat flour", "50 g Unsweetened cocoa powder", "1 tsp Baking soda", "0.5 tsp Salt", "100 g Unsalted butter, softened", "150 g Coconut sugar", "1 large Egg, raw", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "120 ml Low-fat milk", "200 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "50 g Powdered sugar", "1 tsp Lemon juice"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C (350°F) and line baking sheets with parchment paper. In a medium bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt. In a separate large bowl, cream together the softened unsalted butter and coconut sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until well combined. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with the low-fat milk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined, being careful not to overmix. Drop rounded tablespoons of batter onto the prepared baking sheets, about 5 cm apart. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the cakes cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. While the cakes are cooling, prepare the frosting. In a small bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, powdered sugar, and lemon juice until smooth and creamy. Once the cake rounds are completely cooled, spread or pipe about 1-2 tablespoons of the frosting onto the flat side of one cake round, then gently top with another cake round to form a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining cake rounds and frosting.

title: Whole Wheat Banana Oat Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Frosting
ingredients_json: ["200 g Whole wheat flour", "100 g Rolled oats", "50 g Almond flour", "10 g Baking powder", "2 g Cinnamon, ground", "1 g Salt", "100 g Ripe bananas, mashed", "60 ml Maple syrup", "60 ml Unsweetened almond milk", "30 ml Coconut oil, melted", "1 piece Egg, large", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "200 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "30 g Powdered erythritol", "5 ml Lemon juice"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C (350°F) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, rolled oats, almond flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. In a separate medium bowl, mash the ripe bananas until smooth. Whisk in the maple syrup, almond milk, melted coconut oil, egg, and vanilla extract until well combined. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined, being careful not to overmix. Drop rounded tablespoons of the batter onto the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 5 cm (2 inches) between each cookie. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. While the cookies are cooling, prepare the frosting. In a small bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, powdered erythritol, and lemon juice. Stir until smooth and creamy. Once the cookies are completely cooled, spread a generous amount of the Greek yogurt frosting onto the flat side of one cookie and gently top with another cookie to form a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining cookies. Store the whoopie pies in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

title: Whole Wheat Apple Cinnamon Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Frosting
ingredients_json: ["190 g Whole wheat flour", "100 g Rolled oats", "80 g Erythritol", "2 tsp Baking powder", "1 tsp Ground cinnamon", "0.5 tsp Ground nutmeg", "0.25 tsp Salt", "120 g Unsweetened applesauce", "60 g Plain Greek yogurt, 2%", "60 ml Unsweetened almond milk", "30 ml Melted coconut oil", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "1 piece Egg, large", "100 g Unsweetened shredded coconut", "150 g Plain Greek yogurt, 2%", "30 g Powdered erythritol", "1 tsp Lemon juice", "0.5 tsp Vanilla extract"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C (350°F) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, rolled oats, erythritol, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. In a separate medium bowl, combine the unsweetened applesauce, 60g of Greek yogurt, almond milk, melted coconut oil, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract. Whisk the egg in a small bowl and then add it to the wet ingredients, stirring until just combined. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until a thick batter forms, being careful not to overmix. Fold in the unsweetened shredded coconut. Drop rounded tablespoons of the batter onto the prepared baking sheets, about 2 inches apart. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. While the cookies are cooling, prepare the frosting. In a medium bowl, combine the remaining 150g of Greek yogurt, powdered erythritol, lemon juice, and 0.5 teaspoon of vanilla extract. Stir until smooth and creamy. Once the cookie halves are completely cool, spread about 1 tablespoon of the Greek yogurt frosting onto the flat side of one cookie half and gently press another cookie half on top to form a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining cookie halves and frosting.

title: Whole Wheat Banana Oat Whoopie Pies with Cream Cheese Frosting
ingredients_json: ["150 g Whole wheat flour", "100 g Rolled oats, ground", "1 tsp Baking soda", "0.5 tsp Ground cinnamon", "0.25 tsp Salt", "60 g Unsalted butter, softened", "100 g Coconut sugar", "2 large Eggs, room temperature", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "2 medium Bananas, mashed (about 180g)", "120 g Cream cheese, softened", "30 g Powdered sugar", "0.5 tsp Lemon juice"]

Mix in the mashed bananas until well combined. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. Do not overmix. Drop rounded tablespoons of batter onto the prepared baking sheets, about 2 inches apart. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for 2 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. While the cookies are cooling, prepare the frosting. In a small bowl, beat the softened cream cheese, powdered sugar, and lemon juice until smooth and creamy. Once the cookies are completely cooled, spread a dollop of cream cheese frosting onto the bottom of one cookie and top with another cookie, pressing gently to create a sandwich.
